Hi all — quick note from ops: Gmail has two common issues here:

1) If a recipient forwards an event from their calendar instead of the original invitation, Google sometimes converts the time to the forwarder’s local zone *and* drops the timezone metadata (aka "floating" event). That means the invite displays at the same clock time for the forwarder but a different clock time for others.

2) Daylight Saving differences around March can make conversions look off if the event was created with a non-DST-aware zone label.

Best workaround is: the host should re-send the event as an .ics with explicit TZIDs (e.g., America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Singapore) or create two separate invites with the same meeting link but anchored to different time zones. Also ask recipients to check the event details in the calendar (three-dot menu -> "Event details") to confirm the timezone.

Jordan — if you want, I can generate a timezone-anchored .ics for Amit and attach it here.

— Marissa
